items.title: Three false job failures fixed
items.headline: Screener, repair and watchdog jobs no longer report failures that were not real problems.
items.summary: systemctl --user --failed on 2026-10-07 lists four failed units, and three of them are defects in this repository
added: The watchdog's uv cache-lock check counts the lock as held only when some process holds it exclusively. Shared holders are uv run processes, which hold the lock shared for their whole lifetime and block no other uv invocation. They read as not held and reset the held-since state, so back-to-back long jobs never accumulate into a "stuck" reading.
A healer code-fix attempt whose worktree no longer exists after the agent run is recorded as a failed fix ("worktree removed during the agent run"). It never aborts the healer run.

Every scheduled unit that publishes the dashboard through investor.web_publish declares the analyst-target credibility outputs that the publish refreshes as volatile paths: data/analyst_target_quality.jsonl and reports/analyst_targets/.

items.title: Index funds scored fairly on fees
items.headline: Index funds are now scored only on their fee level, since outperformance claims do not apply to them.
items.summary: FundFeeImpact skips the alpha-justifies-fee adjustment when the holding's fund_type is passive_fund, so the fee band alone scores it
added: Fund Fee Impact (±300): scores the annual_fee_pct fee band (<0.3% +150, <0.6% +50, <1.0% −50, <1.5% −150, else −300). When three_year_alpha_pct is known it adds +200 if alpha exceeds the fee and −150 otherwise, except for a fund_type: passive_fund holding. That holding scores the fee band alone, because an index fund's alpha is tracking difference plus cost (openspec/strategy/passive_fund.md). Alpha Delivery still scores it.

items.title: Data watchlist respects stated ready dates
items.headline: Waiting items are no longer marked stale before the date they said they would be ready.
items.summary: data_watch_is_stale() in investor.project_setup.openspec_gate: an entry over 14 days old is STALE only if it is also more than 14 days past every ISO date in its ready condition

items.title: Detailed timings for the decision step
items.headline: The daily log now shows how long each part of the stock-decision step takes, helping find slowdowns.
items.summary: decide_universe accepts an optional stage timer and starts a named step at each internal boundary: fetch, quality_gate, sentiment_inputs, score_batch, podcast_signals, expert_panel, surge, disclosure_and_portfolio, and decision_loop
added: The pulse completion row in data/daily_run_log.jsonl records decide_universe_stage_seconds: wall-clock seconds for each internal step of the universe decision stage (fetch, quality_gate, sentiment_inputs, score_batch, podcast_signals, expert_panel, surge, disclosure_and_portfolio, decision_loop).
The breakdown is a separate field from stage_seconds. The slow-stage health check over stage_seconds does not read it.
Each finished step is logged as it closes, so a run killed by its timeout still leaves the finished steps' timings in the journal.

items.title: Weekly podcast summary now has real data
items.headline: The weekly podcast summary had been empty for eight weeks because it could not see the analysed podcast signals. It can now.
items.summary: The weekly podcast summary (data/weekly_analysis/<week>-podcast-summary.md, written by the report job) has reported signal_count: 0 and "No signals in this period" for every week from W34 to W41
added: The enriched podcast signal store (data/podcasts/backtest) is host-local state. It is whitelisted in investor.worktree.SHAREABLE_PATHS and shared into the job worktrees that use it: investor-podcast-daily, which enriches into it, and investor-report, whose weekly podcast summary reads it. A job that uses it from an unshared worktree sees an empty store, which publishes an empty podcast summary and re-enriches every signal from scratch on each run.

No path whitelisted for sharing may contain a git-tracked file. A shared path replaces the worktree's copy with a symlink, and a tracked file makes the checkout create that copy, so the share fails. A test enforces this over the whole whitelist.

items.title: Real bid-ask spread logged on decisions
items.headline: Each decision now records the actual buy-sell price gap seen, giving a truer picture of trading costs.
items.summary: The cost-vs-edge kill-test (scripts/evaluate_cost_vs_edge_killtest.py, IDEAS 20261005-04) found mean 13-week net-of-cost excess return negative in every conviction band
added: Every decision scored from live market data records the quoted book seen at fetch time in technical_snapshot: quoted_bid, quoted_ask and quoted_spread (ask − bid as a fraction of the mid). Each field is null when the provider gives no positive quote on that side; quoted_spread is also null for a crossed quote.
The quoted book is audit-only. It never contributes to a category score, the composite, the action, or the conviction.

A cost-vs-edge evaluation over decision rows uses a row's logged quoted_spread when present, falls back to a price-range spread proxy only for rows logged before the field existed, and reports what share of its sample used the quoted spread.

items.title: Weekly report keeps accounting-quality signal
items.headline: Weekly report entries now carry the earnings-quality signal, fixing a gap in its coverage.
items.summary: t5_accrual_quality_signals_7d reads 65% (630/975) and is graded a MISS against its ≥65% band
added: The weekly report's "Weekly report YYYY-MM-DD: <action>" re-log rows record the accrual-quality signal too (T5). A re-log row written for a scored ticker whose accrual tier is present carries the same zero-delta Signal(name="accrual_quality") in signals_used[], with the raw ratio and tier, as the engine's own decision row. A ticker with no accrual tier carries no such signal.

items.title: Evidence check reads full decision history
items.headline: The independence check on evidence now reads every monthly decision log, not just one file.
items.summary: Read every file from iter_audit_files(path), oldest first
added: The evidence-independence lineage inventory reads every rotated decision-audit file, oldest first. Its audit digest is the SHA-256 of those files' bytes concatenated in that order, which equals the single-file digest when the audit is unrotated.

items.title: Old decision log no longer silently read empty
items.headline: A test now catches code reading the outdated decision log, and the screener's re-evaluated decisions are saved to the right file.
items.summary: Readers that open the legacy data/decision_audit.jsonl directly have silently read an empty log since monthly rotation
added: The test suite fails when package code reads the legacy single decision-audit file directly, or hands that path to a function that reads its path argument directly, instead of going through the rotated-file helpers. Exceptions are an explicit, reasoned allowlist.
Decisions logged by the screener's surge re-evaluation are written to the current month's rotated audit file, the same file the decision engine's default writer uses.
The ticker-resolution backfill audits every rotated decision-audit file. Its correction keys identify the file and the line within that file.

items.title: Every dashboard reads the full decision history
items.headline: Weekly picks, screener and analytics now read all monthly decision logs, and gaps in the daily picks history are backfilled.
items.summary: Add audit_log.decisions.iter_audit_lines(base_path)
added: Every reader of the decision audit spans the rotated monthly audit files, oldest first, and falls back to the single legacy file only when no monthly file exists. No reader may silently read an empty log because the legacy path stopped being written. This covers the weekly-picks daily points, the screener's latest decision per ticker, the index-boundary and seasonality analytics, the pulse dashboards, and the sigma-barrier re-resolution.

The daily weekly-picks points ledger has no gap for a day with decision rows. Days missed because of a reader defect are backfilled from the audit with the fixed reader. Each ticker gets one ledger row per day, ranked on its latest decision of that day.

items.title: Experimental signals must be pre-registered
items.headline: A check ensures any experimental signal being scored has a frozen test plan, and checks now read the full decision history.
added: A research shadow manifest invariant (T5). Any shadow category with a scored assessment in the last 7 days of decision-audit shadow_category_scores must have a frozen evaluation manifest in data/shadow_evaluations/. A scored category without one fails the invariant, and the failure names the category.

The product invariants read the decision audit across every rotated monthly audit file, not the legacy single file. A check judged on audit rows never silently evaluates an empty log because of rotation.

items.title: More operating figures saved with each snapshot
items.headline: Each fundamentals refresh now saves revenue, costs, margins, receivables, cash flow and more, dated as known at the time.
items.summary: Add a second declarative line set, OPERATING_LINES, to the existing generic capture in investor.fundamentals.statement_lines
added: A second statement-line set, the operating set, is captured on every fundamentals refresh. It covers total revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, SG&A, R&D, operating income, pretax income, tax provision, net income, inventory, accounts receivable, accounts payable, stockholders' equity, operating cash flow, capital expenditure, and depreciation and amortization. Each line has ordered label fallbacks. The set is persisted per fiscal-year end on the fundamentals snapshot, and therefore point-in-time in the fundamentals history.

The operating set follows the same rules as the financing set. A missing or non-finite cell is recorded as missing and never as zero. Each fiscal year records the lines present and the reporting currency. The lines take part in the content fingerprint. A capture failure never suppresses an otherwise valid snapshot, and it never suppresses the financing set.

items.title: Stop-loss price logged on buy decisions
items.headline: Every buy decision now records its stop-loss price, 1.5 times typical daily range below entry.
items.summary: Decision rows log price_at_analysis and technical_snapshot.atr_pct, but not the stop-loss the 1.5 × ATR rule implies
added: Every BUY and COND_BUY decision records stop_loss_price: the stop-loss rule's price, entry − 1.5 × ATR at the decision's price_at_analysis, to at least four decimal places. It is null on other actions and when the price or ATR is unavailable.
A reader that shows a decision's stop-loss uses the logged stop_loss_price when present. It recomputes from price_at_analysis and atr_pct only for rows logged before the field existed.

items.title: Expensive active funds flagged for trimming
items.headline: Active funds with high fees and no proven outperformance, or with outperformance below their fee, now read at least trim.
items.summary: T1 portfolio_annual_fee_drag_sek reads 3,905 SEK/yr against a target of ≤1,728 SEK/yr (MISS)
added: A holding with fund_type: active_fund reads at least TRIM on the T15 long-term recommendation when either exit condition in openspec/strategy/active_fund.md holds: - its annual_fee_pct is ≥1.5% and it has no researched three_year_alpha_pct; or - its researched three_year_alpha_pct minus annual_fee_pct is ≤0.

The floor only lowers an action (ACCUMULATE or HOLD becomes TRIM). It never turns an EXIT back into a TRIM, and it never applies to a holding that is not active_fund. An unclassified fund is never floored on its fee alone.
A floored recommendation's rationale names the floor, the action the score alone would read, the triggering condition (fee and alpha), and openspec/strategy/active_fund.md.

items.title: More precise price-range figure on decisions
items.headline: The daily price range share is now recorded to four decimals, so stop-loss levels derived from it are accurate.
items.summary: decision_engine logs technical_snapshot.atr_pct to 4 decimals
added: A decision's technical snapshot records the ATR share of price to at least four decimal places, so a stop-loss derived from it (entry − 1.5 × ATR) is accurate to well under 0.1% of price.

items.title: Order ticket shows its entry price basis
items.headline: The dashboard reads the engine's own decision, not report re-entries, and the ticket labels its entry price and any stop difference.
items.summary: The weekly report re-logs one audit row per ticker (reasoning=["Weekly report <date>: <action>"])
added: Dashboard surfaces read the engine's own decision rows. The weekly report's re-log rows (reasoning "Weekly report <date>: <action>") are never treated as a ticker's latest decision.

The execution ticket labels the price it sizes from as the decision's entry. It shows the weekly report's buy band only as labelled context, and states when the band's stop differs from the decision stop.

items.title: Stale-price count limited to relevant stocks
items.headline: The count of unsettled prices now covers only stocks you screen or hold, avoiding misleading alarms.
items.summary: market_data.stale_provisional_bar_count() takes an optional tickers scope
added: The stale-provisional-bar count reported on the bars-coverage metric covers only the tickers that metric measures (screened or held). Provisional bars of a ticker that has left that set are not counted, because no refresh will ever settle them.

items.title: Conviction labels show hit rate everywhere
items.headline: Every conviction label across the dashboard now shows the measured 13-week hit rate for that level and how it was measured.
items.summary: Move the inbox's label logic into one shared component, web/src/components/ConvictionLabel.tsx
added: Every conviction label the dashboard shows is accompanied by that band's measured 13-week hit rate and its basis. This covers the Decision Inbox, the per-stock page, the decisions table, the stocks table and the weekly memo action cards. The display rules are those of the Decision Inbox: clustered basis when it clears the floor, otherwise pooled with its count, marked provisional when right-censored, and the bare label when the band has no resolved outcomes.

items.title: Order ticket sized from the engine's decision
items.headline: The stock page's ticket now uses the engine's suggested weight, your measured capital and a 2% loss cap instead of fixed numbers.
items.summary: The "Advisory order execution ticket" on the per-stock page (web/src/views/Stock.tsx, added in 5e359b8c4) computed its own sizing in the browser, ignoring what the engine decided
added: The per-stock advisory execution ticket sizes a position from the logged decision. Position value is the decision's suggested weight × measured T1 total personal capital, at the decision's entry price. The stop follows the stop-loss rule: 1.5 × the decision's logged ATR below the decision's entry price, or else the weekly report band's 1.5 × ATR stop. The outcome-grading barrier is never used as a stop. Shares are capped so the loss to that stop is at most 2% of T1 (T2). The ticket shows the sizing basis and whether the T2 cap bound.

The ticket never substitutes a fixed capital figure, a percentage stop or a position-size cap of its own. When measured T1, a stop below entry or a suggested weight is unavailable, it states that sizing is unavailable and names the missing input.
The per-stock export carries the decision's entry price and stop.

items.title: Decision Inbox shows hit rate per conviction
items.headline: Each HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label in the inbox now comes with its measured 13-week hit rate and how reliable that figure is.
items.summary: The Decision Inbox conviction column shows a bare HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW label (web/src/components/DecisionInbox.tsx)
added: Every conviction label in the Decision Inbox is shown with that band's measured 13-week hit rate and its basis. The cohort-matched, ticker-clustered rate is used when the band clears the distinct-ticker floor. Otherwise the pooled rate is shown, labelled pooled, with its resolved count. The label is marked provisional when the band's outcomes are right-censored. A band with no resolved outcomes shows the bare label.
The exported calibration status carries each band's clustered hit rate, computed the same way as the t12_conviction_*_hit_rate_clustered health metrics (absent when it is not measurable).

items.title: Filing analysis can resume where it stopped
items.headline: The daily filing analysis, which used to run out of time with nothing to show, can now continue from where it left off.
items.summary: The daily pulse's graphrag_extraction stage has used its full 600s budget every run since stage timings started (2026-09-30..2026-10-05: 638, 605, 605, 603, 601, 601s) and has produced nothing

items.title: Weekly memo suggests fee-saving switch
items.headline: When total fund fees exceed target, the memo adds one action to switch the costliest fund, showing the fee, yearly cost and saving.
items.summary: When the portfolio's fee drag exceeds the T1 target, the memo appends one SWITCH action, after the ranked trades and outside the five-trade cap, for the holding with the largest SEK/yr fee drag
added: When the portfolio's total annual fee drag exceeds the T1 fee-drag target, the weekly memo SHALL append exactly one SWITCH action after its ranked trades, outside the trade cap. The action is for the holding with the largest SEK/yr fee drag whose fee exceeds the reference index-fund fee. It states the fee, its SEK/yr cost, the portfolio total against the target, and the saving at the reference fee. It names no replacement fund and carries a memo-<date>-<ticker>-SWITCH journal action id. Within target, or with no fee data, no SWITCH action is emitted.

items.title: Annual fee shown on each fund holding
items.headline: Each fund holding card now shows its fee, yearly cost in kronor, share of total fee drag and your target.
items.summary: Every Long-term Holdings card for a holding with a researched non-zero annual_fee_pct gains one line
added: Each Long-term Holdings card for a holding with a researched, non-zero annual fee SHALL state the fee percentage, its annual cost in SEK, its share of the portfolio's total annual fee drag, and the T1 fee-drag target (- Annual fee: <pct>% ≈ <SEK>/yr (<share> of portfolio fee drag <total> SEK/yr; T1 target ≤<target> SEK/yr)). Holdings with no fee or a 0.0 placeholder carry no such line, and an unreadable holdings registry omits the line without failing the report.

items.title: Podcast verdicts shown on report cards
items.headline: Report cards now show the podcast consensus beside the scored podcast category, marked as not affecting the score.
items.summary: When a stock carries a podcast_consensus shadow score, the card's Category scores line appends PodcastVerdict*=<signed> [shadow; effective 0] after the scored categories
added: A recommendation card's signed Category scores line SHALL show the podcast verdict consensus shadow (podcast_consensus) as PodcastVerdict*=<signed> [shadow; effective 0] whenever the stock carries one, after the scored categories and outside the composite sum, so a card whose printed podcast verdicts contradict the scored Podcast category shows both readings. The Screened Universe table columns are unchanged.

items.title: Podcast buy and sell consensus tracked
items.headline: The app now measures whether podcast hosts lean bullish or bearish on each stock over 30 days. Tracked for testing, not used in scores yet.
items.summary: The scored podcast category (±100 of the composite) is fed by one QualitativeSignal per ticker (scoring.set_podcast_category)
added: The system SHALL compute a point-in-time podcast verdict consensus per ticker from the LLM-extracted episode verdicts (data/podcasts/signals/*.yaml): the strength-weighted bullish (BUY) minus bearish (SELL, AVOID) verdicts divided by the directional verdict count, scaled to ±100. Strength weights are strong 1.0, moderate 0.6, weak 0.3.

Only episodes published in the 30 days strictly before the as-of date count; HOLD and WATCH verdicts carry no direction. A ticker with no directional verdict in the window has no consensus (absence, not zero).

The consensus SHALL be scored as the SHADOW universe component podcast_consensus (weight 0.0, ±100, unreplayable) and recorded on every audit row, so its live rank IC is measured beside the scored podcast category on the same rows. It never moves the composite, an action, or a size.

Pre-registered verdict: replacing the keyword source of the scored podcast category with the consensus requires a live h=1 cross-sectional IC of at least +0.03 with t ≥ +2 over ≥ 26 non-overlapping weekly sections, above the scored podcast category's IC over the same weeks, and lands in its own proposal. A t ≤ 0 at 26 sections kills it.
